item.title: Gold holds above $5,000 as stronger dollar, thin holiday trading weigh
item.description:
Gold prices edged lower in early trading on Monday but held above the $5,000-per-ounce mark as a stronger dollar and profit-taking weighed on the precious metal following last week's inflation-driven rebound. Trading volumes remained thin with U.S. markets closed for Presidents Day and Chinese exchanges shut for Lunar New Year celebrations.

Spot gold slipped 0.4% to around $5,020 per ounce in early Monday trading, according to The Business Times. The pullback came after the metal recovered from mid-week lows near $4,880 to close above $5,040 on Friday, buoyed by softer-than-expected U.S. inflation data.

item.title: ByteDance to add safeguards to Seedance 2.0 after Hollywood backlash
item.description: The Walt Disney Company has accused ByteDance of large-scale intellectual property theft, sending a cease-and-desist letter to the Chinese tech giant over its newly launched AI video generator Seedance 2.0. The tool, released on Thursday, February 12, has drawn rapid condemnation from Hollywood studios and creative organizations, prompting ByteDance to pledge stronger safeguards.

item.title: India opens AI summit as first major Global South host
item.description:
India kicks off one of the largest artificial intelligence gatherings ever staged as Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurates the India AI Impact Summit 2026 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on Monday. The five-day event, running from February 16 to 20, is the first major global AI summit to be hosted in the Global South, positioning India as a central voice in shaping the future of the technology.

The summit brings together approximately 20 heads of state and government, including French President Emmanuel Macron, Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis, and Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, along with ministerial delegations from over 45 countries. United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres and senior officials from multiple international organizations are also participating.

item.title: Rubio backs Orban reelection bid during Hungary visit
item.description:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio traveled to Budapest on Monday to meet with Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban, signing a civilian nuclear cooperation agreement and delivering a strong endorsement of the embattled leader just weeks before Hungary's April 12 elections. Rubio told Orban that President Donald Trump is "deeply committed to your success" and that Orban's continued leadership is in America's national interest.

The high-profile visit comes as Orban and his Fidesz party face their most difficult electoral challenge since retaking power in 2010. Opposition leader Peter Magyar's center-right Tisza party leads in most polls, with a recent Idea Institute survey showing Tisza at 48% among committed voters compared to 38% for Fidesz.

item.title: Russia offers to halt strikes if Ukraine holds elections
item.description:
Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Galuzin announced Saturday that Moscow is prepared to suspend airstrikes on election day if Ukraine holds presidential polls, reiterating an earlier offer from President Vladimir Putin while questioning the legitimacy of President Volodymyr Zelensky's government.

The announcement comes days before a new round of trilateral talks between Russia, the United States, and Ukraine scheduled for February 17-18 in Geneva, and as Washington continues pressing Kyiv to hold elections as a condition for U.S. security guarantees.

item.title: EU's Kallas rejects US criticism, urges Europe to 'reclaim agency'
item.description:
The 62nd Munich Security Conference concluded Sunday with European leaders sending a clear message: the continent must take greater responsibility for its own defense amid shifting transatlantic dynamics. Over three days of discussions, top officials outlined plans for increased military spending, nuclear deterrence cooperation, and reduced dependence on Washington.

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas rejected American criticism of Europe, pushing back against suggestions that "woke and decadent Europe" faces "civilizational erasure." Speaking at the conference's closing session, Kallas outlined three priorities: defending Europe starting with Ukraine, securing the neighborhood through EU enlargement, and building global partnerships. She warned that Russia "must not gain more at the negotiating table than it has achieved on the battlefield."

item.title: Top fund manager warns most software firms won't survive AI
item.description:
A fund manager whose portfolio has outperformed 99% of competitors is sounding the alarm on software stocks, warning that artificial intelligence poses an existential threat to the industry and that only a handful of companies will survive the coming disruption.

"We think application software faces an existential threat from AI," said Nick Evans, whose $12 billion global technology fund at Polar Capital beat 99% of peers over the past year and 97% over five years, in comments reported by Bloomberg on Sunday.

The warning comes as software stocks have suffered a brutal start to 2026. An exchange-traded fund tracking the U.S. software sector has plummeted more than 21% this year, according to data from S3 Partners, while hedge funds have generated $24 billion in profits by betting against the sector. The software industry has seen roughly $1 trillion wiped from its market capitalization since late January, sparked by fears that AI large language models could disintermediate traditional enterprise applications.

item.title: Cuba activates 1990s-era rationing plan as Trump oil blockade deepens
item.description:
Cuba is facing its most severe fuel shortage since the collapse of the Soviet Union as the Trump administration's oil blockade deepens, prompting the communist government to activate emergency rationing measures while Washington simultaneously delivers humanitarian aid through the Catholic Church.

The Cuban government has announced it is implementing what it calls "Option Zero," a contingency plan conceived during the 1990s Special Period that contemplates extreme rationing, local food self-sufficiency, and the use of animal traction for transport. President Miguel Díaz-Canel recently confirmed the country has entered this phase, pledging to guarantee seven pounds of rice monthly per person while prioritizing locally produced goods.

item.title: Finland warns Russia is building military bases on its border
item.description:
Finnish Defense Minister Antti Häkkänen warned this weekend that Russia is reinforcing its strategic nuclear presence in the Arctic and constructing new military facilities along Finland's border, signaling an intensifying security threat to Europe's northern flank.

"Russia has most of their biggest strategic capabilities in nuclear, submarines, long-range bombers in the Kola Peninsula area," Häkkänen told Euronews on the sidelines of the Munich Security Conference, which concluded Sunday. "They are building new military facilities along our border, the same as during the Cold War. It would be wise to watch the Arctic and build Arctic capabilities."

The Kola Peninsula, a 100,000-square-kilometer region in far northwestern Russia, hosts the majority of the country's sea-based strategic nuclear arsenal, including submarines and long-range aviation assets.

item.title: Italy's Meloni publicly rejects German chancellor's MAGA criticism
item.description:
The alliance between Italy and Germany that emerged as a new force in European politics faces its first test after Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni publicly disagreed with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz over his criticism of the American MAGA movement, exposing divergent visions of transatlantic relations just weeks after the leaders pledged closer cooperation.

"I do not agree" with Merz's remarks against MAGA culture, Meloni told Corriere della Sera and other Italian newspapers on February 15, returning from the African Union Assembly in Addis Ababa. While she endorsed Merz's call for Europe to strengthen its security capabilities and build a "European pillar of NATO," Meloni declined to echo his broader critique of the American political movement.

item.title: Canada moves to bridge EU and Pacific trade blocs
item.description:
Prime Minister Mark Carney is pursuing negotiations to forge links between the European Union and the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), a move that could unite nearly 40 nations in a coordinated framework to counter American protectionism.

Politico reported Monday that the Canadian government is spearheading talks between the 27-member EU and the 11-nation CPTPP to explore harmonized "rules of origin" that would allow manufacturers across both blocs to trade goods and components more smoothly through a mechanism called cumulation. If formalized, this arrangement would create an integrated trade architecture spanning both sides of the globe, designed to reduce vulnerability to tariff threats from Washington.

item.title: NASA targets Feb. 19 for second Artemis II fueling rehearsal
item.description: NASA announced Monday that it is targeting February 19 for a second wet dress rehearsal of its Artemis II moon rocket after hydrogen fuel leaks and ground equipment issues disrupted testing earlier this month. The setbacks have pushed the earliest possible launch date to March 6, while ongoing concerns about the Orion capsule's heat shield continue to draw scrutiny from some space safety experts.

item.title: Google DeepMind says AlphaFold now used by 3 million researchers
item.description:
Google DeepMind leaders revealed this weekend that the company's AI-powered protein structure database has reached more than 3 million researchers across 190 countries, a milestone that underscores how artificial intelligence is reshaping scientific discovery worldwide.

In a commentary published in Fortune ahead of the India AI Impact Summit, DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis and Google Senior Vice President James Manyika outlined how the freely available AlphaFold Protein Database has become a standard tool for scientists tackling pressing global challenges. More than one-third of those researchers are based in low- and middle-income countries, according to the executives.

item.title: BHP signs $4.3B silver streaming deal with Wheaton Precious Metals
item.description:
BHP Group has entered into a $4.3 billion silver streaming agreement with Wheaton Precious Metals, marking what the mining giant describes as the largest streaming deal to date by upfront value.

Under the agreement announced Tuesday alongside BHP's half-year results, the Australian miner will deliver silver from its 33.75% stake in Peru's Antamina mine to Wheaton in exchange for an upfront payment of $4.3 billion at completion. Upon closing, expected on or about April 1, 2026, Wheaton will receive a combined 67.5% of all silver produced from Antamina, doubling its current exposure from the 33.75% it already receives under an existing stream with Glencore.

item.title: Trash piles up in Havana as US oil sanctions cripple Cuba
item.description:
Garbage is piling up on street corners across Havana, attracting swarms of flies and emitting the stench of rotting food, as Washington's campaign to cut off oil supplies to Cuba cripples the capital's waste collection system.

Only 44 of Havana's 106 garbage trucks remain operational due to fuel shortages, state media outlet Cubadebate reported this month, according to Reuters. Cardboard boxes, plastic bottles, used bags, and rags now tower at intersections throughout the coastal city, forcing motorists, pedestrians, and cyclists to navigate around the refuse.

"It's all over the city," resident Jose Ramon Cruz told Reuters. "It's been more than 10 days since a garbage truck came."

item.title: NASA says 15,000 city-killer asteroids remain undetected
item.description:
NASA's head of planetary defense has acknowledged that approximately 15,000 medium-sized asteroids capable of devastating an entire city remain undetected and untracked, leaving Earth vulnerable to a potentially catastrophic strike with little warning.

Dr. Kelly Fast, the agency's Acting Planetary Defense Officer, made the admission at the American Association for the Advancement of Science annual meeting in Phoenix, Arizona, which concluded on February 14. She said NASA has only identified about 40 percent of the estimated 25,000 near-Earth asteroids that are at least 140 meters in diameter, the threshold scientists consider capable of causing major regional devastation.

"It's truly the asteroids we are unaware of that keep me up at night," Fast said. "We aren't particularly concerned about the larger ones featured in movies since we know their locations. The smaller objects are constantly entering our atmosphere, and I'm not excessively worried about them. It's the intermediate-sized asteroids that could cause regional damage—while not necessarily global consequences—that truly concern us. And we have no idea where all of them are."

item.title: Trump to participate 'indirectly' in Iran nuclear talks in Geneva
item.description:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in Geneva on Monday ahead of a second round of indirect nuclear negotiations with the United States, meeting with the head of the U.N. nuclear watchdog as both sides signaled cautious willingness to engage while holding firm to core positions.

The talks, scheduled for Tuesday and mediated by Oman, come amid heightened military posturing in the Persian Gulf and volatile commodity markets. President Donald Trump said he would participate "indirectly" in the negotiations, calling them "very important" while asserting that Tehran is eager to reach a deal following U.S. strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities last June.

item.title: Report finds 74% of Big Tech's AI climate claims lack evidence
item.description:
A new analysis has found that the vast majority of claims from technology companies about artificial intelligence's potential to combat climate change are unsupported by evidence, with researchers warning that the energy-intensive nature of generative AI may actually worsen global emissions.

The report, released on February 17 by climate nonprofits Beyond Fossil Fuels and Climate Action Against Disinformation, examined 154 statements from industry and institutional sources claiming AI would deliver net climate benefits. According to the study, 74 percent of these assertions lacked any verifiable evidence.

item.title: Oil holds steady as US-Iran nuclear talks resume in Geneva
item.description:
Oil prices held steady on Tuesday as traders weighed supply disruption risks following Iranian naval exercises near the Strait of Hormuz, with attention focused on high-stakes nuclear talks between the United States and Iran set to begin later in the day in Geneva.

Brent crude futures edged lower by 0.2 percent, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate held near Monday's closing levels, according to Reuters. Market participants are watching whether the negotiations could ease tensions or set the stage for further escalation in a region that accounts for roughly a fifth of global oil shipments.

item.title: China's clean energy capacity surpasses fossil fuels for first time
item.description:
China has crossed a historic threshold in its energy transition, with clean energy sources now accounting for more installed power capacity than fossil fuels for the first time, according to new data from Global Energy Monitor. As of February 2026, 52% of China's operating power capacity comes from non-fossil fuel sources, while 48% is derived from coal, natural gas, and other fossil fuels.

The milestone places the world's largest carbon emitter alongside Brazil, France, and Germany as economies predominantly powered by clean energy. Yet China's continued construction of coal-fired power plants at record levels underscores the tensions between its climate ambitions and energy security concerns.
